title: Work & study
goal: Talk about jobs, school and the office, and say what you can, can't, must and don't have to do.
intro: This unit covers ability and obligation. Tamil distinguishes **being able** (**முடியும்** *muḍiyum* 'it is possible') from **knowing how** (**தெரியும்** *teriyum* 'it is known'), and expresses **must** with the ending **-ணும்** *-ṇum*. Note that the 'able' person is in the instrumental case: **என்னால முடியும்** 'by me it is possible' = 'I can'.

vocab.note: spoken: டீச்சர் ṭīcchar; address: சார் / மிஸ் / டீச்சர்
spoken: கத்துக்கோ kattukkō; present கத்துக்கிறேன் kattukkirēn
negative முடியாது muḍiyādu; with instrumental: என்னால ennāla

phrases.native: நான் ஒரு ஐடி கம்பெனியில வேலை பாக்கிறேன்.
phrases.roman: nān oru aiṭi kampeniyila vēlai pākkirēn.
phrases.en: I work in an IT company.
Can you (do you know how to) drive a car?
You don't have to come tomorrow.

grammar.title: Can: முடியும் (ability/possibility) and தெரியும் (know how)
grammar.body:
**முடியும்** *muḍiyum* means 'it is possible'. The person who is able goes in the **instrumental** case **-ஆல** *-āla* (written -ஆல்): **என்னால**, உன்னால, உங்களால, அவரால. The action is in the **infinitive** (-அ form): **என்னால வர முடியும்** 'I can come'. Negative: **முடியாது**. In speech the instrumental is often dropped: வர முடியாது 'can't come'.

For **skills** — knowing how to do something — use **தெரியும்** with the dative: **எனக்கு நீச்சல் தெரியும்** 'I can swim', **எனக்கு கார் ஓட்டத் தெரியும்** 'I know how to drive'.

**Permission** ('may I?', 'you may') uses **-லாம்** *-lām* (written -கலாம்): வரலாமா? 'may I come?', போலாம் 'you may go / let's go'.

examples.en: I don't know how to cook.

grammar.title: Must / have to: -ணும்; don't have to: -அ வேணாம்
grammar.body:
Obligation and need are expressed by adding **-ணும்** *-ṇum* (written -க வேண்டும்) to the infinitive: போ → **போகணும்** 'must go', படி → **படிக்கணும்** 'must study', வா → **வரணும்** 'must come'. It doesn't change for person. The same form also means 'want to' when the subject is in the dative: **எனக்குப் போகணும்** 'I want / need to go'.

**'Don't have to'** = infinitive + **வேணாம்**: நீங்க வர வேணாம் 'you don't need to come'. **'Mustn't'** = **-க்கூடாது**: இங்க புகைபிடிக்கக்கூடாது 'you mustn't smoke here'.

Past obligation: infinitive + **வேண்டியிருந்துச்சு** 'had to': வேலை பாக்க வேண்டியிருந்துச்சு 'had to work'.

examples.en: The exam is tomorrow; I must study hard today.
You have to come to the office at nine sharp.
You mustn't talk on the phone in class.
Yesterday I had to work late.

dialogue.title: Asking for leave
dialogue.setting: Karthik asks his manager, Mrs Revathi, for a day off.

lines.speaker: Karthik
lines.native: வெள்ளிக்கிழமை எனக்கு லீவு வேணும் மேடம். ஊருக்குப் போகணும்.
lines.roman: veḷḷikkiḻamai enakku līvu vēṇum mēḍam. ūrukkup pōgaṇum.
lines.en: I need leave on Friday, madam. I have to go to my home town.

lines.speaker: Revathi
lines.en: But there's an important meeting on Friday.

lines.speaker: Karthik
lines.native: தெரியும் மேடம். ஆனா என் தங்கச்சிக்குக் கல்யாணம். கண்டிப்பா போகணும்.
lines.roman: teriyum mēḍam. ānā en tangacchikkuk kalyāṇam. kaṇḍippā pōgaṇum.
lines.en: I know, madam. But it's my younger sister's wedding. I really have to go.

lines.speaker: Revathi
lines.native: ஓ, வாழ்த்துக்கள்! அப்போ ரிப்போர்ட்டை வியாழக்கிழமைக்குள்ள முடிக்க முடியுமா?
lines.roman: ō, vāḻttukkaḷ! appō rippōrṭṭai viyāḻakkiḻamaikkuḷḷa muḍikka muḍiyumā?
lines.en: Oh, congratulations! Then can you finish the report by Thursday?

lines.speaker: Karthik
lines.en: Yes, madam. I'll finish it by tomorrow itself.

lines.speaker: Revathi
lines.native: சரி, லீவு எடுத்துக்கோங்க. திங்கக்கிழமை சரியா வந்துடணும்.
lines.roman: sari, līvu eḍuttukkōnga. tingakkiḻamai sariyā vanduḍaṇum.
lines.en: All right, take the leave. You must be back on Monday without fail.

lines.speaker: Karthik
lines.en: Definitely, madam. Thank you very much!

culture: Education is highly valued in Tamil Nadu, and board exam results in '10th' and '12th standard' are big family events. Teachers are addressed as சார் or மிஸ் / டீச்சர், and students stand when a teacher enters. Office culture mixes Tamil and English freely — 'meeting', 'leave', 'report', 'boss' are all used in Tamil sentences.

tip.title: Talking about your job
tip.body:
- 'I'm a teacher' needs no verb: **நான் ஒரு டீச்சர்**.
- 'I work (as…)': **வேலை பாக்கிறேன்**: **இன்ஜினியரா** வேலை பாக்கிறேன் 'I work as an engineer'.
- Most job titles are said in English: டீச்சர், இன்ஜினியர், டிரைவர்; lawyer is **வக்கீல்**.
- Ask politely: **நீங்க என்ன வேலை பாக்கிறீங்க?**

sentences.en: I'm a teacher.
Are you a teacher?
Mum is a teacher at a school.
My elder brother works as an engineer.
Her father is a lawyer.
Our grandfather is a farmer.
He works in the police.
Our driver didn't come today.
What does your father do for a living?

lessons.title: At the office

tip.title: Have to: -ணும்
tip.body:
- Add **-ணும்** to the verb's infinitive for 'must, have to': போ → **போகணும்**, வா → **வரணும்**, முடி → **முடிக்கணும்**.
- It never changes for the person: நான் / நீங்க / அவங்க **போகணும்**.
- With **எனக்கு** it means 'I want to': எனக்குப் போகணும்.

new: நான் ஒரு ஐடி கம்பெனியில வேலை பாக்கிறேன்.

sentences.en: I have to go to the office early tomorrow.
I need to see the boss today.
All the staff have to come to the meeting.
I have to finish this report today.
What time do I have to be at the office?
I need to call you after the meeting.
I have a lot of work to do at the office today.
This month's salary hasn't come in yet.
He's in business.
The bus is really crowded.

tip.title: Don't have to, mustn't
tip.body:
- 'Don't have to' is infinitive + **வேணாம்**: வர **வேணாம்** 'no need to come'.
- 'Mustn't' is infinitive + **-க்கூடாது**: பேச**க்கூடாது** 'you mustn't talk'.
- 'Have to' is still **-ணும்**: படிக்**கணும்**.
- Don't mix them up: வேணாம் is relaxed, கூடாது is a rule.

sentences.en: I have to study three subjects for the exam.
Don't watch TV, kiddo, you have to study.
You mustn't make noise in class.
No looking at phones in the exam.
You don't have to come to class on Saturday.
No need to study today, it's a holiday!

sentences.native: எல்லா மாணவரும் ஒன்பது மணிக்கு ஸ்கூல்ல இருக்கணும்.
sentences.roman: ellā māṇavarum onbadu maṇikku skūlla irukkaṇum.
sentences.en: All students must be at school by nine.
My younger brother is in tenth grade.
My elder sister is at university.
Which subject do you like?

tip.title: Can: என்னால … முடியும் · know how: எனக்கு … தெரியும்
tip.body:
- Being able: **என்னால** + infinitive + **முடியும்**: என்னால வர **முடியும்** 'I can come'; can't = **முடியாது**, couldn't = **முடியல**.
- Knowing how (a skill): **எனக்கு** + infinitive + **தெரியும்**: எனக்கு ஓட்டத் **தெரியும்** 'I can drive'.
- Note the person: **-ஆல** with முடியும் (என்னால, உங்களால), **-க்கு** with தெரியும்.
tip.pattern: என்னால + verb-அ + முடியும்  ·  எனக்கு + verb-அ + தெரியும்

sentences.en: Can you do this job?
I can't walk that far.

sentences.native: பை ரொம்பக் கனமா இருக்கு, என்னால தூக்க முடியல.
sentences.roman: pai rombak ganamā irukku, ennāla tūkka muḍiyala.
sentences.en: The bag is too heavy, I couldn't lift it.
Can you fix the computer?
I know computers well.
Mum can't speak English.
I can ride a scooter.
I'm learning Tamil now.
Will you teach me Tamil?
Dad taught me to swim.

tip.title: May I? -லாமா
tip.body:
- Verb + **-லாமா?** asks permission: **போலாமா?** 'may I go?', **உக்காரலாமா?** 'may I sit?'.
- The answer drops the -ஆ: **போலாம்** 'you may go'.
- Leave from work is **லீவு**: லீவு **எடுக்கலாமா?** 'can I take leave?'.
- Add சார் / மேடம் to make it polite at work.

sentences.en: Madam, may I go now?
Can I take leave tomorrow?
All right, you may go.
May I sit here?
Sir, may I ask something?
Can I work from home today?
I'm not well, I can't come in today.
The meeting is at ten sharp.
I'm going to my home town for the Pongal holidays.
